summary: Ten comment-endorsed discoveries spanning developer tools, practical programming reading, NES games, and whisky glassware.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 front-page stories fully crawled | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Protomaps
items.source_story_title: Protomaps: Self-hosting map tiles has gotten cheap and easy
items.summary: Open-source, self-hosted maps; a user praises low running costs and easy theming.
items.why_included: A concrete migration away from an unexpectedly large Google Maps bill backs the recommendation.
items.evidence: joshstrange switched from Google Maps and praises Protomaps for low cost, theming, and ease of use.

evidence_sources.author: joshstrange
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Protomaps and absolutely love it. After getting hit with a Google Maps bill that was larger than I ever would have expected, I swapped it out for Protomaps instead and I’ve loved it ever since. Dirt cheap to run, theme-able, easy to use.

items.name: Skald
items.source_story_title: A NES emulator written in Odin
items.summary: Declarative GUI framework for Odin; praised for performance, though not fully featured.
items.why_included: First-hand use supports a promising niche GUI framework, with its immaturity made explicit.
items.evidence: christophilus used Skald and finds it performant and relatively light on resources, but not fully featured.

evidence_sources.author: christophilus
evidence_sources.excerpt: For the record, the library I used was Skald[0]. It's decent. Not 100% fully featured yet, but performant and fairly low resource, especially compared to Quickshell.

items.name: Emacs For Mac OS X
items.summary: Ready-to-install macOS Emacs builds; a user praises the straightforward DMG experience.
items.why_included: A specific distribution earns direct first-hand praise rather than a generic editor mention.
items.evidence: LordGrey uses these Emacs builds and reports an up-to-date, easy DMG installation and a great experience.

evidence_sources.author: LordGrey
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use Emacs For Mac OS X. Up to date and installs via a .dmg. Great experience.

items.name: veriexec
items.source_story_title: Disk encryption on NetBSD – achieving secrecy
items.summary: NetBSD executable-verification subsystem; a user reports that pre-execution checks work well.
items.why_included: A practical, first-hand recommendation surfaces an overlooked operating-system security feature.
items.evidence: jmclnx recommends veriexec for validating executables before they start and says it worked in personal use.

evidence_sources.author: jmclnx
evidence_sources.excerpt: You can use veriexec to validate executables prior them starting. I have used it and it works fine.

items.name: 500 Lines or Less
items.summary: Programming book walking through compact projects, from initial design to implementation.
items.why_included: An independent comment endorses the whole book beyond the submitted 3D-modeller chapter.
items.evidence: forgotpwd16 praises the Architecture of Open Source Applications collection and singles out 500 Lines or Less as the most enjoyable.

evidence_sources.author: forgotpwd16
evidence_sources.excerpt: The entire "Architecture of Open Source Applications" is amazing, and among those "500 Lines or Less" is imo the most enjoyable.

items.name: Making a 3D Modeler, in C, in a Week
items.summary: Daniel Hooper’s ShapeUp write-up explains building an SDF-based 3D modeler in a week.
items.why_included: The comment explicitly recommends the engineering write-up, not merely the modeler it describes.
items.evidence: jasonjmcghee calls Daniel Hooper’s ShapeUp write-up a great read and highlights the small implementation and week-long build.

evidence_sources.author: jasonjmcghee
evidence_sources.excerpt: Another great read is Daniel Hooper’s write up on his SDF 3D modeler ShapeUp.

items.name: Ali Rahimi’s NIPS 2017 Test of Time Award speech
items.source_story_title: Understanding Positional Embeddings in Modern LLMs
items.summary: Machine-learning talk challenging alchemy-like experimentation; explicitly recommended in the positional-embeddings discussion.
items.why_included: A clear recommendation points to a concrete talk about the gap between ML practice and understanding.
items.evidence: nsagent identifies Rahimi’s award speech, recalls its machine-learning-as-alchemy argument, and highly recommends watching it.

evidence_sources.author: nsagent
evidence_sources.excerpt: I presume your comment is in reference to this speech, as he famously states: "Machine Learning has become alchemy" in it. For anyone who has some time and hasn't watched it, I'd highly recommend it.

items.name: Witch n' Wiz
items.summary: Modern NES puzzle-platformer; a fan calls it a favorite and recommends it to puzzle lovers.
items.why_included: An enthusiastic, specific player recommendation emerged from a targeted raw-thread pass.
items.evidence: sourceror calls Witch ‘n Wiz a favorite, compares it to Catrap, and highly recommends it for puzzle-game fans.

evidence_sources.author: sourceror
evidence_sources.excerpt: Highly recommend it if you’re into puzzle games. I’d say that in retrospect, this is the game that is responsible for starting my interest in retro-emulation.

items.name: Little Sisyphus
items.summary: Physics-based NES platformer about hauling a ball up a mountain; playable in-browser.
items.why_included: An explicit alternative-game recommendation leads to a directly playable creator page.
items.evidence: SandmanDP highly recommends Little Sisyphus among modern NES games omitted from the article’s list.

evidence_sources.author: SandmanDP
evidence_sources.excerpt: Two modern NES games not on this list that I would also highly recommend: Little Sisyphus

items.name: Norlan Whisky Glass
items.source_story_title: A quest to create the perfect whiskey glass
items.summary: Double-walled whisky glass; a former owner praises it but balks at replacement cost.
items.why_included: First-hand praise comes with a concrete value caveat rather than unqualified product hype.
items.evidence: epiccoleman praises the Norlan glasses they owned, but says replacing them is too expensive for their current interest in whisky.

evidence_sources.author: epiccoleman
evidence_sources.excerpt: $32 for one glass is too much for me to stomach given my middling level of interest in whiskey these days, and a rocks glass is good enough. But they were damn fine glasses.
